title: Set Up eM Client
cardText: Set up IMAP, POP, Microsoft 365 and Exchange email accounts in eM Client.
Configure incoming and outgoing servers, authentication and POP message retention.
Safely migrate old POP messages, PST archives and eM Client backups while preventing duplicate mail.
text: This guide covers eM Client email setup on Windows and macOS.
Use automatic configuration where supported, or manually enter the provider's IMAP, POP and SMTP settings.
IMAP and Exchange normally restore server-stored messages and folders automatically.
Check for locally stored POP messages, Local Folders, archives and contacts that are not available on the server.
Use eM Client Backup and Restore when moving an entire existing installation.
Use the Import wizard for selected Outlook PST, MBOX, EML and other supported mail archives.
Import into separate folders or data files where supported, check for duplicates and merge only missing messages.
Preserve original mail backups until migration is verified.

identifySetupType.title: Identify the email setup
body: Determine whether this is a new mailbox setup or a migration from an existing computer.
Identify the previous email application and account type.
IMAP and Exchange normally synchronise server-stored messages.
POP and Local Folders may contain messages stored only on the original computer.
Preserve the original email installation if local mail must be transferred.

identifyExistingClient.title: Identify the original email application
body: Determine whether the source is eM Client, classic Outlook, Thunderbird, Apple Mail or another email client.
Check whether the account uses IMAP, Exchange or POP.
Inspect the original application for Local Folders and separate archives.
If the original application is eM Client, determine whether the entire database should be transferred.
If the original application is different, identify its available backup or export format.
Keep the original installation available until migration is verified.

backupExistingEmClient.title: Back up the original eM Client installation
body: Open eM Client on the original computer.
Use Menu, Backup to start a full application backup.
In older versions, the command may be under Menu, File, Backup.
Check the backup destination under Menu, Settings, General, Backup.
Allow the backup to finish completely.
Locate the resulting ZIP backup, commonly stored in the user's Documents, eM Client folder unless configured otherwise.
Copy the backup to separate, reliable storage.
Keep an untouched copy throughout the migration.
Full backups are particularly important for POP messages, Local Folders, contacts and locally stored archives.

link.name: eM Client: Automatic Backups
link.description: Explanation of backup requirements for POP and local mail.

backupOtherClient.title: Back up email from another application
body: Identify the original application's mail storage and export format.
For classic Outlook, locate any PST files containing POP messages and local archives.
For Thunderbird, back up its profile or export the required MBOX or EML messages.
For Apple Mail, use its supported mailbox export procedure where appropriate.
Check whether all required messages already exist in webmail.
Preserve local-only mail and any separate archives.
Keep an untouched backup of the original source data.

link.name: eM Client: Import from Other Email Clients
link.description: Official information about supported application and file imports.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Mail
link.description: Official PST export instructions.

protectOriginalMail.title: Protect the original email data
body: The required original mail or application data has not been backed up successfully.
Keep the original computer and email application unchanged.
Preserve POP messages, Local Folders, Sent Items and separate archives.
Create a verified backup before removing accounts or restoring another database.
Do not overwrite the only working copy of existing mail.
Continue after protecting the source data.

chooseExistingMigration.title: Choose complete restoration or selected mail transfer
body: Determine whether the user wants the complete previous eM Client installation restored.
A full backup can preserve the application database, accounts, settings and local data.
A complete database restore is different from importing selected messages into an existing mailbox.
If the destination eM Client already contains important mail or settings, back it up first.
Do not restore an entire old database over a working installation simply to recover a few messages.
Use selected mail export and import when the destination should retain its existing setup.

restoreEmClientBackup.title: Restore an eM Client backup
body: Install a compatible eM Client version on the destination computer.
If the destination already contains important data, back it up before restoring.
For a replacement installation, skip initial account setup where appropriate.
Transfer the original eM Client backup ZIP to the destination computer.
Open eM Client and select Menu, File, Restore.
Select the correct backup file or configure its location under Settings, General, Backup.
Allow the database restoration to complete.
Restart eM Client if required and activate the appropriate licence.
Check locally stored POP messages, Local Folders, contacts and other restored data.
Allow IMAP or Exchange accounts to reconnect and synchronise.
Do not import the same messages again unless the restored database is missing required data.

link.name: eM Client: Transfer Data to Another Computer
link.description: Official step-by-step Backup and Restore procedure.

link.name: eM Client: Restore Backups
link.description: Official backup recovery guidance.

verifyRestoredDatabase.title: Verify the restored eM Client database
body: Confirm the expected email accounts and application settings are present.
Check old POP messages and Local Folders.
Open a selection of older messages and attachments.
Verify contacts, calendars and local archives where required.
For IMAP or Exchange, allow server synchronisation and compare with webmail.
Check for repeated or duplicated folders before importing anything else.
If the restored installation contains everything required, no separate mail import is needed.
Keep the original backup for future recovery.

collectAccountDetails.title: Identify the provider and account settings
body: Obtain the complete email address and provider information.
Determine whether the account uses Microsoft 365, Exchange, IMAP or POP.
For manual setup, obtain the incoming server hostname, SMTP server hostname, ports and encryption requirements.
Confirm whether the provider supports OAuth or requires another authentication method.
Check that the selected protocol is enabled for the account.
Use current provider documentation rather than guessing mail server settings.

link.name: eM Client: IMAP and POP3 Protocols
link.description: Official information about manual setup and protocol differences.

link.name: eM Client: Getting Started
link.description: Official account setup and provider information.

obtainProviderSettings.title: Obtain the correct provider settings
body: The required account configuration is not available.
Check the email provider's official setup instructions.
Record the incoming and outgoing servers, ports, encryption and authentication method.
Confirm that the provider permits the selected POP, IMAP or Exchange connection.
Do not disable encryption or use unsupported authentication methods.
Continue once the settings are confirmed.

addEmailAccount.title: Add an email account to eM Client
body: Open eM Client.
On a new installation, use the initial account setup wizard.
On Windows, open Menu, Accounts and select Add account.
On macOS, open eM Client, Accounts and select Add account.
Enter the email address and use Automatic Setup where supported.
Complete the provider's sign-in procedure and any multifactor authentication.
For Microsoft 365, Exchange and supported services, use the provider's recommended account type.
If automatic detection fails or manual POP or IMAP is required, use the Mail, Other account setup route.

link.name: eM Client: Account Setup
link.description: Official instructions for adding an email account.

manualAccountSetup.title: Configure IMAP or POP manually
body: Open Menu, Accounts, Add account on Windows, or eM Client, Accounts, Add account on macOS.
In the New Account window, select Mail, Other.
Enter the email address and proceed to the incoming server configuration.
Choose IMAP or POP3 according to the provider's requirements.
Enter the incoming server hostname and the required username.
Enter the outgoing SMTP server and authentication details when prompted.
Use the provider's actual server settings, ports and connection security.
Common encrypted ports are IMAP 993, POP 995 and SMTP submission 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with SSL/TLS.
Complete the configuration test and follow any provider authentication prompts.
Do not choose POP simply because an automatic IMAP setup failed.

link.name: eM Client: IMAP and POP3 Setup Guide
link.description: Official manual account configuration walkthrough.

manualAccountSetup.alt: eM Client incoming server setup showing POP3 and IMAP protocol options
manualAccountSetup.caption: Choose POP3 or IMAP and enter the incoming server settings supplied by the email provider.

configureImap.title: Complete IMAP configuration
body: Check the provider's incoming IMAP server hostname.
Confirm the required port and encryption, commonly port 993 with SSL/TLS.
Check outgoing SMTP settings, authentication and encryption.
Complete any OAuth or multifactor authentication prompts.
Finish account setup and allow eM Client to retrieve the server mailbox folders.
If folders are missing, check account settings and synchronisation before attempting any mail import.

link.name: eM Client: IMAP Protocol Guide
link.description: Official IMAP account configuration instructions.

configurePop.title: Complete POP account configuration
body: Check the incoming POP server hostname.
Use the provider's documented port and encryption, commonly port 995 with SSL/TLS.
Configure outgoing SMTP server settings and supported authentication.
Complete the setup and confirm the account connects.
Recognise that POP downloads mail and does not synchronise normal mailbox folders between devices.
Preserve the existing POP database or archive if moving from another computer.
Review message retention before relying on the new POP account for mail downloads.

link.name: eM Client: POP3 Protocol Guide
link.description: Official POP configuration and behaviour.

configurePopRetention.title: Review POP message retention
body: Open the POP account settings in eM Client.
Find the POP server settings and review options for keeping downloaded messages on the server, where offered.
Check whether server copies are removed after a specified period or when messages are deleted.
Record the existing retention policy before changing it.
During a migration, retaining server copies temporarily can reduce the risk of another computer removing mail before the replacement receives it.
Monitor mailbox storage because leaving all messages on the server indefinitely may fill the mailbox.
Confirm that new messages are downloaded and stored as intended.
Keep the original local POP mail backup.

link.name: eM Client: IMAP and POP3 Protocols
link.description: Official information about POP downloads and account settings.

testEmailConnection.title: Test sending and receiving
body: Send a plain test email to another accessible account.
Reply from that account and confirm the response arrives in eM Client.
Check the outgoing message appears in Sent.
Check for authentication, connection and synchronisation errors.
For POP, confirm incoming messages download as expected.
After testing, identify whether the account synchronises from the server or uses local POP storage.

troubleshootSetup.title: Investigate account connection errors
body: Record the exact error displayed by eM Client.
Confirm the correct incoming and outgoing mail servers.
Check ports, encryption and authentication against the provider's settings.
Verify POP or IMAP access is enabled by the provider.
Check OAuth and multifactor authentication requirements.
For business accounts, confirm the selected connection type is permitted by the organisation.
Compare account access through webmail.
Correct the identified issue before testing again.

link.name: eM Client: Troubleshooting
link.description: Official account connection and database troubleshooting.

checkAccountSyncType.title: Does the mailbox synchronise from the server?
body: Check the configured account type in eM Client.
IMAP, Exchange and supported Microsoft 365 connections normally synchronise server-stored messages and folders.
POP accounts may store downloaded messages only in the local eM Client database.
For IMAP or Exchange, verify server synchronisation before importing old mail.
For POP, check whether historical mail must be transferred from a previous computer or application.

verifyServerSyncedMail.title: Verify IMAP or Exchange synchronisation
body: Allow eM Client to synchronise the mailbox.
Compare Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Archive and custom folders with the provider's webmail service.
Check older messages and attachments.
Make sure the correct account and folders are selected.
If a message exists in webmail but not eM Client, investigate synchronisation rather than importing an archive.
If all server-stored mail is present, check for Local Folders and other data that would not automatically synchronise.

link.name: eM Client: IMAP and POP Differences
link.description: Explanation of mailbox synchronisation and local storage.

investigateSyncMissing.title: Find the source of missing messages
body: Check whether the missing messages are present in webmail.
Search Archive, Deleted Items and custom server folders.
If the messages exist on the server, check synchronisation status, folder visibility and account settings.
If messages are absent from webmail but exist in the original application, check its local archives.
Do not import an entire old mailbox simply to fix a synchronisation problem.

troubleshootImapSync.title: Investigate eM Client synchronisation
body: Confirm the application is connected to the correct email account.
Check folder visibility, synchronisation errors and account authentication.
Allow large mailboxes additional time to synchronise.
Check that the expected messages are available in webmail.
Investigate the account connection instead of importing PST or MBOX files.
Retest the missing folders after correcting the issue.

checkMissingMailSource.title: Are the missing messages stored locally?
body: Inspect the original email client and any locally stored archives.
Check previous POP accounts, Local Folders, PST files and other message exports.
If required messages exist locally but not on the server, protect them before migration.
If the messages are absent from both the server and source computer, check backups or the provider.
Do not import unrelated mail files as a workaround.

checkLocalOnlyData.title: Are there local-only folders or archives?
body: Inspect the original email installation for mail that is not visible in webmail.
Check eM Client Local Folders, separate Data Files, old POP mail and archive folders.
Check contacts, calendars and other locally stored data separately.
IMAP synchronises server-stored mail but does not automatically transfer local archives.
If all required mail is synchronised and no additional local data is needed, no import is necessary.
If locally stored messages are required, preserve them before continuing.

checkPopMigration.title: Check whether old POP mail must be transferred
body: Determine whether this is a new POP account or a replacement for an existing installation.
Check old Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders.
POP cannot automatically restore messages previously removed from the provider's server.
Compare the old locally stored messages with those visible in the new installation.
If everything required is already available, no further import is needed.
If old local mail is required, verify the backup before migration.

confirmLocalBackup.title: Verify the local mail backup
body: Identify the original POP mailbox, Local Folders or separate archive files.
For eM Client, confirm a completed full-database backup or a supported export of the required local data.
For another application, verify its PST, MBOX, EML or other supported mail export.
Keep an untouched backup separate from files used during import.
Confirm that the required messages and folders are included.
Do not begin an import until the original data is protected.

link.name: eM Client: Backup and Restore
link.description: Official full-database backup instructions.

link.name: eM Client: Import Other Mail
link.description: Supported import formats and applications.

identifyImportSource.title: Identify the original mail format
body: Determine whether the source is an eM Client backup, Outlook PST, MBOX, EML or another supported application.
A full eM Client backup restores the application database rather than selectively importing mail.
A PST archive can be imported without requiring Outlook to be installed.
eM Client also supports imports from several other email clients and message formats.
If a full backup must be combined with an existing destination installation, avoid an uncontrolled database restore.
Choose a method that preserves existing destination data.

link.name: eM Client: Import from Microsoft Outlook
link.description: Official guidance for direct PST imports.

link.name: eM Client: Supported Import Formats
link.description: Official information about application and file imports.

checkDestinationMailbox.title: Check the destination mailbox before importing
body: Compare the source archive with the messages already present in eM Client.
Check Inbox, Sent, Archive and important custom folders.
Compare a sample of messages using sender, recipient, date, subject, contents and attachments.
Look for overlap between old POP mail and messages already synchronised from the server.
Check the destination mailbox's remaining storage.
Do not import old messages directly into populated folders if duplication is possible.
Prepare a separate destination for inspecting the imported messages first.

prepareImportStaging.title: Prepare a separate import destination
body: Use a separate location named Imported Old Mail for staging imported messages.
Enable Local Folders where necessary under Menu, Settings, General, Folders.
For supported eM Client versions, consider a separate eM Client Data File for PST archives.
A separate Data File keeps historical messages isolated from the active mailbox.
For other import formats, choose a separate Local Folders destination where supported.
If the import wizard cannot isolate the messages, cancel and use another supported method.
Do not directly merge an unreviewed source into populated Inbox or Sent folders.
A staging location does not automatically deduplicate messages.

link.name: eM Client: Local Folders
link.description: Official instructions for enabling and using Local Folders.

link.name: eM Client: Separate Data Files
link.description: Official information about creating separate local mail archives.

chooseImportMethod.title: Choose the appropriate import method
body: Use the Outlook PST importer if the source is a PST file.
Use the supported application or MBOX/EML importer for other message formats.
If the source is a full eM Client backup, Restore may be appropriate only when replacing an installation or restoring into a protected destination.
Do not restore a full database over existing important mail merely to access a few old messages.
Select an import destination that keeps the source messages separate.
Avoid running the same import twice without checking the first result.

importOutlookPst.title: Import Outlook PST mail
body: Preserve an untouched backup of the PST.
In eM Client on Windows, select Menu, File, Import.
On macOS, use File, Import.
Choose the Outlook or Outlook Data File import option available in the installed version.
Select the preserved PST file.
eM Client can import directly from PST without requiring Outlook to be installed.
Check the available destination options before starting.
Where supported, import the PST as a separate Data File rather than merging directly into an active mailbox.
If the feature is unavailable, select an isolated folder where the importer permits it.
Do not import directly into populated Inbox or Sent folders without reviewing existing messages.
Continue by selecting only the source folders that are required.

link.description: Official PST import instructions and destination options.

link.name: eM Client: Import PST as a Data File
link.description: Official procedure for creating an isolated EMDF archive from PST data.

importOutlookPst.alt: eM Client Import wizard showing the Outlook Data File PST import option
importOutlookPst.caption: Select the Outlook PST source and use a separate Data File or staging destination where supported.

selectImportFolders.title: Select only the required folders
body: Review the folders available within the source PST.
Select the Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders that contain required historical mail.
Exclude unnecessary or already migrated folders where appropriate.
Check whether the destination preserves the original folder structure.
Select a separate Data File or other isolated destination where supported.
Avoid importing directly into an existing populated folder.
Complete the import and allow the operation to finish.
Check where the messages were actually imported before making another attempt.
Keep the original PST backup unchanged.

link.name: eM Client: Outlook Import Wizard
link.description: Official folder selection and destination instructions.

selectImportFolders.alt: eM Client Outlook Import wizard showing selectable folders within a PST archive
selectImportFolders.caption: Choose only the folders required and review their destination before importing.

importOtherMail.title: Import mail from another client or format
body: Open eM Client and select Menu, File, Import on Windows, or File, Import on macOS.
Choose the supported source application or message file format.
For Thunderbird, use the available application import option where supported.
For MBOX or EML files, use the corresponding file import option.
For previous eM Client data, choose a supported import or restoration method without overwriting existing important messages.
Select only the required messages and folders where the importer permits it.
Import into a separate staging folder or data file where supported.
If isolation is not possible, stop before merging into populated folders.
Complete the import and check its destination.
Do not repeat the import until the first result has been reviewed.

link.name: eM Client: Import Wizard
link.description: Official supported import sources and formats.

link.name: eM Client: Import Other Email Clients
link.description: Official application migration guidance.

checkPartialImport.title: Check a failed or incomplete import
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire import.
Inspect the staging folder or separate Data File.
Determine which messages and folders have already transferred.
Compare completed date ranges and message counts with the original archive.
Check storage capacity, unsupported items and any import errors.
Correct the identified problem before retrying.
Use a new clearly labelled staging location or import only the missing messages if another attempt is needed.
Preserve the original source and partial import.

reviewImportedMail.title: Review imported mail for duplicates
body: Open the Imported Old Mail folder or separate Data File.
Compare the imported messages with Inbox, Sent, Archive and important custom folders.
Check sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments.
Do not assume messages with the same subject are identical.
Look for old POP messages that are missing from the destination mailbox.
Identify overlapping mail before merging folders.
Avoid bulk deletion based only on matching dates or subjects.
Keep the original archive and imported staging area intact while comparing.

resolveImportDuplicates.title: Resolve duplicate or missing messages
body: Compare suspected duplicate messages carefully with existing destination items.
Use message contents and attachments to distinguish actual duplicates from different messages in the same conversation.
Only remove a redundant staging copy after verifying the required message exists elsewhere.
For missing messages, inspect the original archive and any folders excluded from the import.
Use smaller batches for large imports.
Do not assume the Import wizard automatically removes every duplicate.
If the result is uncertain, leave the imported messages in the separate staging area.
Keep the original backup unchanged.

chooseMailDestination.title: Keep the archive separate or copy into the mailbox
body: Decide whether the imported mail should remain in a separate historical folder or Data File.
If the user only needs access to older messages, leaving them in a separate archive may be sufficient.
If messages must appear across devices, they need to be copied into the synchronised mailbox where supported.
Check server mailbox storage before uploading large archives.
Do not merge the entire imported archive into an existing Inbox or Sent folder without reviewing it.
Keep the source and staging backups until verification is complete.

copyMailToServer.title: Copy reviewed mail into a server mailbox
body: Confirm the destination IMAP or Exchange account is connected and synchronising.
Create a separate Imported Old Mail folder under the destination account.
Copy selected messages or folders from the local staging area into the separate server folder.
Work in manageable batches for large archives.
Monitor synchronisation and mailbox storage.
Check webmail to verify that uploaded messages are present.
Do not copy directly into populated Inbox or Sent folders before duplicate review.
Keep the original local archive and backup.

checkPartialUpload.title: Check incomplete server uploads
body: Do not repeat the entire upload immediately.
Compare the server staging folder with the original local source.
Check which messages are already visible in webmail.
Investigate mailbox quotas, connection errors and oversized attachments.
Correct the problem and transfer only missing messages where possible.
Use another clearly labelled staging folder if the existing result is uncertain.
Retain local source files and backups.

chooseMergeMethod.title: Keep the server archive separate or merge
body: Decide whether Imported Old Mail should remain a separate archive folder within the IMAP or Exchange account.
Keeping it separate avoids altering existing Inbox and Sent folders.
If normal folder placement is required, identify which messages are not already present in the destination.
Copy only missing messages into their appropriate folders.
Do not rely on automatic duplicate removal during the merge.
Preserve staging and source copies until verification.

mergeReviewedMail.title: Merge only missing messages
body: Identify messages that do not already exist in Inbox, Sent, Archive or the relevant custom folder.
Copy only those required messages from the staging folder.
Work in manageable batches.
Allow the mailbox to synchronise completely.
Check the resulting messages and attachments through webmail where available.
Do not delete the staging archive or original files until the results are verified.
If duplicates or missing mail appear, return to the review process.

verifyMigratedMail.title: Verify migrated messages and folders
body: Compare the migrated messages with the original mailbox or archive.
Check Inbox, Sent, Archive, Imported Old Mail and custom folders.
Open older messages and verify their attachments.
Check message dates and folder organisation.
Look for unexpected duplicates after any merge.
For IMAP or Exchange, verify mail intended for the server appears in webmail.
For POP or local archives, confirm the messages remain accessible locally.
Check contacts and calendars separately when required.
Keep the original database or exported mail backup until verification is complete.

migrationEscalation.title: Further eM Client migration required
body: The old mail could not be transferred or reconciled safely.
Preserve the original eM Client backup, PST or other source archive.
Keep partial imports separate.
Record the account type, source format, import method and any errors.
Check database compatibility, corrupted files, storage quotas and synchronisation.
If an import was partially completed, identify transferred messages before attempting it again.
Do not merge uncertain message sets or delete source files.
Use the provider's supported recovery or import procedure.

link.description: Official information about recovering or importing mail data.

link.name: eM Client: Troubleshooting
link.description: Official support for account and database problems.

setupComplete.title: eM Client setup completed
body: The email account can send and receive messages.
Incoming and outgoing server settings are configured correctly.
For IMAP or Exchange, required server-stored messages and folders have synchronised.
If no local-only data is missing, no mail import was required.
For POP, local mail storage and server retention have been reviewed.
Any required old mail or database data has been restored, imported or preserved as a separate archive.
Imported messages have been checked for duplicates before merging.
Check contacts, calendars, signatures and rules separately where required.
Keep verified backups of important locally stored messages.

setupEscalation.title: Further eM Client account diagnostics
body: The email account cannot connect after checking its server settings.
Record the eM Client version, email provider, protocol and exact error.
Confirm that the selected connection and authentication methods are supported.
Check OAuth, multifactor authentication and organisational restrictions.
Compare mailbox access through webmail.
Use the Email Not Working guide for further mail delivery troubleshooting.
Preserve existing POP, Local Folders and database backups.

link.name: eM Client: Troubleshooting
link.description: Official account and application troubleshooting documentation.
